newsitem.title: USA: Bio-Logic says Q2 won't be as strong as Q1.
newsitem.headline: Bio-Logic says Q2 won't be as strong as Q1.

text.p: Bio-Logic Systems Corp, which earlier reported a profit for the first quarter, said it does not expect results to be as strong in the second quarter.

"While we're extremely pleased with our performance during the first quarter, we must keep in mind that the summer months are traditionally a slower sales period, therefore, we don't expect second quarter results to be quite as strong," said Chief Executive Gabriel Raviv.

Earlier, the maker of computerized medical equipment said it earned $224,978, or $0.06 a share, in the first quarter compared to a loss of $281,640, or $0.07 a share, a year ago. Sales rose to $4.4 million from $2.8 million.

The rise in sales represented a dramatic rebound from the 22 percent decline in sales reported in the first quarter last year, the company said. The decline a year ago was due to a reorganization of the company's sales force.
Bio-Logic said international sales rose 110 percent to $1.3 million in the first quarter of fiscal 1998, compared with $624,132 in the same period last year.
